concept: Avatar shows a person or an owner the way a device shows a reading: a small window cut into the body that holds a picture or one or two letters. It names who and does nothing else, so it is a window and never a key.

default_to_avoid.pattern: round coloured disc with white initials on a hashed background colour, a status dot on its corner
default_to_avoid.why_not: A raised round disc reads as a key that can be pressed, a hashed hue spends colour on a label, and a corner dot repeats a state the row already prints.

default_to_avoid.pattern: round photo with a head-and-shoulders silhouette as the empty state
default_to_avoid.why_not: The silhouette is a drawn figure from a stock kit, not a reading; an empty window should say nothing.

references.source: Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): figures read inside windows cut into the body
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a station name printed in a small window beside the scale
system/FORM.md display class: window recessed into the body, nesting in the body's corner

derivation.consequence: the window is recessed into the body (inverse light)
derivation.form: The window takes surface.sunken and elevation.well, laid over the picture too, so a photo reads as seen through a hole and not stuck on.

derivation.consequence: the window is a rounded rectangle whose radius nests in the body
derivation.form: The window is a rounded square on corner.media, never a disc, so a person never looks like a round key; the picture is clipped inside the ring so its corner is the outer radius minus the ring.

derivation.consequence: one grotesk, regular and medium only
derivation.form: Initials are printed in the one grotesk in medium weight at three sizes, one per window size, with a line box tall enough for Thai marks.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: Every window is the same grey plastic with ink, whoever it shows; there is no hashed hue and no orange.

derivation.consequence: the model name is never the only identifier
derivation.form: A picture is never the only identifier of a person: the name is printed beside it, or the window carries a label.

variants.reason: C is the recessed window already used by Input, Display and Stepper, so a person reads as a reading; A is a raised disc that looks like a key and sits oddly beside the real keys of a row, and B is a plain ring that is the generic avatar and has no depth of its own.

root.why: The window is a recess in the body: sunken plastic, a hairline ring and the inverse light. It is a span, not a button, so nothing in it is pressed.

image.why: The picture fills the window and is clipped by its ring, so its corner nests in the window's radius.

initials.why: One or two letters in medium ink, centred in the window; the line box has room above and below for Thai vowel and tone marks.

mark.why: With no picture and no name the window shows one printed dash, a reading of nothing, instead of a drawn figure.

data-size=sm.why: The small window is 32px with the caption size, for a row of dense text; it is not pressed, so it needs no 44px target.

data-size=md.why: The medium window is 44px with the label size, level with the row of controls beside it.

data-size=lg.why: The large window is 80px with the title size, for the head of a profile or a device card.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the ring draws in the text colour and the inset shadow is dropped, so the window keeps a real edge.
